July 23, 1972
Public Health: p27 cites that accidents involving use of ORVs are on the increase. The noise levels involved, according to National Hoosier Forest DEA p.ll, are such that they will damage even the operator of the ORV and the problem will be compounded by ORV users running in groups. The noise involved will definitely interfere with the enjoyment of those who are out to walk and walking is a very healthy leisure activity. Many hikers are at present discouraged by interference with minibiles and disillusion with this sport is reported by our members.
The existence of ORV trails will have an adverse effect upon non-ORV users. It will hasten to make our nation one of people who do not know how to use legs. It will be even more consequential at a time when many young people are just beginning to discover the joy of backpacking and going out into nature.
A 7.5 billion Federal Aid Highway Act of 1972 was reported to Public Works Committee on July 21, 1972. This would include funds for an increased safety program, improved emergency medical care for victims of accidents (will these funds help victims of ORV use accidents). But most of all the proposal would allow the use of Highway Trust funds money for mass transportation.
At a time when the need for a mass transportation system has become quite clear for many reasons, one of which is cutting down on air pollution, the internal combustion engine will be invading our public lands. Ford Motor Company was forced into complying with the standards set by EPA for emission control. But Japanese make bicycles will be polluting those parts of our public lands were people would like to go for peace and solitude and to get away from the traffic and noises of the city. Encouragement of this industry would result from opening the lands; what appears "controllable" at the present will become a nightware. The graneral public and the future generations will pay for it - later.
Indiana Presaires Audubon Society is a young organization. It was founded in December 1970 and has since then grown to a membership of a region. It is growing at a rapid rate. New chapters are a right; up everywhere and National Audubon is growing at a rate of 3000-4000 members a month. We feel these are give heart numbers of people, who have admowledged their interdependence with nature, and who look for protection to the Federal and State Governments.
Ruth II. Reichmann, Irwident Indiana Sagrafras Auduson Soc Reshville, 1.d. 47448
